articles.title: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as CEO, stock rallies 31%
articles.excerpt:
Nvidia's board of directors unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident that he posed no national security risk. Shares of the AI chipmaker rallied 31.43% during Monday’s pre-market session.

President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a "correct and proper decision."

The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his "candor and ability to lead," the company said in a statement.

Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

articles.title: Exits from gold ETFs top $100 billion for 2026, even as inflows remain net positive
articles.excerpt:
Exits from physically-backed gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) for this year topped a record $100 billion last week, while investments continue to be net positive.

Data from the World Gold Council showed that for every dollar invested last week, there was an outflow of $3. Overall, investments in ETFs last week were $1.18 billion, while redemptions were $3.34 billion, leaving inflows net negative at $2.15 billion.

Year-to-date (YTD) redemption crossed a record $100 billion. The record outflow registered so far is $78.27 billion in 2025. With seven weeks to go, exits are already about 30 per cent higher. Investments at $140 billion may not top last year’s record inflows of $167.18 billion.
articles.citation: Exits from gold ETFs top $100 billion for 2026, even as inflows remain net positive — BusinessLine Mkts, 2026-11-23. https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/gold/exits-from-gold-etfs-top-100-billion-for-2026-even-as-inflows-remain-net-positive/article71734916.ece

articles.title: Gold imports into India decline 40% in April-October: CTI
articles.excerpt:
Gold imports into India declined by around 40 per cent in April-October this year compared to the corresponding period last year, with the country purchasing gold worth $24.7 billion during the seven months, Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) Chairman Brijesh Goyal said on Monday.

According to Goyal, India imported gold worth $41.24 billion between April and October 2025, while the figure stood at $24.7 billion during the same period this year, marking a decline of $16.46 billion.

He said the figures reflected a significant reduction in gold purchases during the current financial year.
